arxiv-1603-04787.title: States and channels in quantum mechanics without complex numbers Presented at 21 st International Conference on Applications of Computer Algebra 2015 (ACA2015), July 20-23, 2015, Kalamata, Greece.

arxiv-1603-04787.description: Abstract In the presented note we aim at exploring the possibility of abandoning complex numbers in the representation of quantum states and operations. We demonstrate a simplified version of quantum mechanics in which the states are represented using real numbers only.

Albrow, Sun-Ju Chung, Kyu-Ha Hwang, Chung-Uk Lee, Yoon-Hyun Ryu, In-Gu Shin, Yossi Shvartzvald, Jennifer C. Yee, Weicheng Zang, Sang-Mok Cha, Dong-Jin Kim, Seung-Lee Kim, Dong-Joo Lee, Yongseok Lee, Byeong-Gon Park, Rich
arxiv-2204-11383.description: Abstract Aims. The light curve of the microlensing event KMT-2021-BLG-0240 exhibits a short-lasting anomaly with complex features near the peak at the 0.1 mag level from a single-lens single-source model. We conducted modeling of the lensing light curve under various interpretations to reveal the nature of the anomaly. Methods.

arxiv-2310-12252.title: Emergent Symmetries and Interactions in High Dimensions: An Isolated Fixed Point Versus A Manifold of Strongly Interacting Fixed Points
arxiv-2310-12252.creator: Fei Zhou
arxiv-2310-12252.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fei Zhou. In this article, we explore conditions of continuous emergent symmetries in gapless states, either as topological quantum critical points (TQCPs) or a stable phase with protecting symmetries and connections to smooth deformations of the gapped states around.

arxiv-2406-17958.title: Local/Short-range conformal field theories from long-range perturbation theory
arxiv-2406-17958.creator: Junchen Rong
arxiv-2406-17958.description: Abstract We show that by imposing the conformal Wald identity, one can extract conformal data of the corresponding short-range/local CFT from the long-range perturbation theory. We first apply this to the O(N) vector model. We demonstrate that by properly re-sum the perturbative series, one gets reasonable estimations of the critical exponents of the local/short-range CFTs.

arxiv-2504-15713.title: Zernike system revisited: imaginary gauge and Higgs oscillator
arxiv-2504-15713.creator: Vahagn Abgaryan, Armen Nersessian, Vahagn Yeghikyan
arxiv-2504-15713.description: Abstract We analyze that recently proposed clasical/quantum mechanical interpretation of Zernike system and establish its equivalence to the Higgs oscillator on sphere or pseudosphere (Lobachevsky plane). We show that the non-reality of the classical Zernike Hamiltonian is an insignificant artifact of imaginary gauge and can be eliminated with a canonical transformation.

arxiv-2505-00916.title: Photoproduction and detection of ρ ′ → π + ​ π − ​ π + ​ π − \rho^{\prime}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{+}\pi^{-} decays in ultra-peripheral collisions and at an electron-ion collider

arxiv-2505-00916.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Neha Devi, Minjung Kim, Spencer R. Klein, Janet Seger. Vector meson photoproduction is an important probe of nuclear structure. Light vector mesons are most sensitive to low − x -x structure, as long as they are not too light for perturbative QCD calculations. The ρ ′ \rho^{\prime} is of interest as an intermediate mass state (between the ρ \rho and J / ψ J/\psi ) that is easier to detect than the ϕ \phi .

arxiv-2507-22136.title: Color as the Impetus: Transforming Few-Shot Learner
arxiv-2507-22136.creator: Chaofei Qi, Zhitai Liu, Jianbin Qiu, Coauthor, Coauthor, Coauthor
arxiv-2507-22136.description: Abstract Humans possess innate meta-learning capabilities, partly attributable to their exceptional color perception. In this paper, we pioneer an innovative viewpoint on few-shot learning by simulating human color perception mechanisms. We propose the ColorSense Learner, a bio-inspired meta-learning framework that capitalizes on inter-channel feature extraction and interactive learning.

arxiv-2508-16172.title: Graph RAG as Human Choice Model: Building a Data-Driven Mobility Agent with Preference Chain
arxiv-2508-16172.creator: Kai Hu, Parfait Atchade-Adelomou, Carlo Adornetto, Adrian Mora-Carrero, Luis Alonso-Pastor, Parfait Atchade-Adelomou, Ariel Noyman, Yubo Liu, Kent Larson
arxiv-2508-16172.description: Abstract Understanding human behavior in urban environments is a crucial field within city sciences. However, collecting accurate behavioral data, particularly in newly developed areas, poses significant challenges. Recent advances in generative agents, powered by Large Language Models (LLMs), have shown promise in simulating human behaviors without relying on extensive datasets.

arxiv-2509-16560.title: Captioning for Text-Video Retrieval via Dual-Group Direct Preference Optimization
arxiv-2509-16560.creator: Ji Soo Lee Byungoh Ko Jaewon Cho Howoong Lee Jaewoon Byun Hyunwoo J. Kim
arxiv-2509-16560.description: Abstract In text-video retrieval, auxiliary captions are often used to enhance video understanding, bridging the gap between the modalities. While recent advances in multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled strong zero-shot caption generation, we observe that such captions tend to be generic and indistinguishable across visually similar videos, limiting their utility for fine-grained retrieval.

arxiv-2601-04393.title: Assessing the quality and coherence of word embeddings after SCM-based intersectional bias mitigation
arxiv-2601-04393.creator: Eren Kocadag
arxiv-2601-04393.description: Abstract Abstract Static word embeddings often absorb social biases from the text they learn from, and those biases can quietly shape downstream systems. Prior work that uses the Stereotype Content Model (SCM) has focused mostly on single-group bias along warmth and competence.

pmc-10731333.creator: Piyatida Molika, Kittinun Leetanaporn, Phetploy Rungkamoltip, Sittiruk Roytrakul, Jitti Hanprasertpong, Raphatphorn Navakanitworakul

pmc-11404030.title: Ethnobotanical study of medicinal plants in Dibatie district, Metekel zone, Benishangul Gumuz Regional State, western Ethiopia
pmc-11404030.creator: Baressa Anbessa, Ermias Lulekal, Asfaw Debella, Ariaya Hymete
pmc-11404030.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundHerbal medicine has been used for the treatment of human and livestock ailments since ancient times. Numerous rural and urban communities in Ethiopia practice traditional medicine and transfer the knowledge verbally from generation to generation. Thus, this study was conducted to document the traditional medicinal plants and associated indigenous knowledge in Dibatie district, Metekel zone, Benishangul Gumuz Regional State, western Ethiopia.MethodsThree hundred seventy-four (374) informants from 11 kebeles (the smallest administrative units) were selected and participated in the data delivery.

pmc-11530650.title: Essential magnetosome proteins MamI and MamL from magnetotactic bacteria interact in mammalian cells
pmc-11530650.creator: Qin Sun, Liu Yu, Sarah C. Donnelly, Cécile Fradin, R. Terry Thompson, Frank S. Prato, Donna E. Goldhawk
pmc-11530650.description: To detect cellular activities deep within the body using magnetic resonance platforms, magnetosomes are the ideal model of genetically-encoded nanoparticles. These membrane-bound iron biominerals produced by magnetotactic bacteria are highly regulated by approximately 30 genes; however, the number of magnetosome genes that are essential and/or constitute the root structure upon which biominerals form is largely undefined.

pmc-11658349.title: Healthy eating patterns associated with reduced risk of inflammatory bowel disease by lowering low-grade inflammation: evidence from a large prospective cohort study
pmc-11658349.creator: Bin Xia, Yan Li, Linmin Hu, Peng Xie, Ningning Mi, Liyuan Lv, Zixin Liang, Yuxuan Sun, Ying Li, Xiaodong Jiang, Guinan Liu, Yuanyuan Feng, Yingxin Zhu, Bo Zhan, Qiangsheng He, Pingguang Lei, Jian Qi, Pengpeng Wang, Jinqiu Yuan
pmc-11658349.description: BackgroundLimited epidemiological evidence exists regarding the role of healthy eating patterns in reducing the risk of Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC). This study aimed to investigate the association between adherence to four established healthy eating patterns and subsequent CD or UC risk, and further examined whether these associations are linked to anti-inflammatory mechanisms.

pmc-12662080.title: Psychometric evaluation of the body uneasiness test in the Arab Gulf region
pmc-12662080.creator: Bernou Melisse, Carine el Khazen, Edwin de Beurs
pmc-12662080.description: IntroductionThe Gulf Cooperation Council is experiencing socio-economic transformations, which coincides with exposure to Western beauty ideals and internalization of the Western thin-ideal, and consequently the development of body uneasiness. The present study psychometrically evaluates the Body Uneasiness Test, suitable for use in the Gulf Cooperation Council.

pmc-12738596.title: Early breastfeeding as protective factor for preschool emotional and behavioral health
pmc-12738596.creator: Susana Vargas-Pérez, Carmen Hernández-Martínez, Núria Voltas, Victoria Arija, Josefa Canals-Sans
pmc-12738596.description: To examine the association between any breastfeeding duration and emotional and behavioral problems in 4-year-old children, considering psychosocial, demographic, and perinatal variables. The sample included 564 children. Any breastfeeding duration was categorized into four groups: no breastfeeding, 1–4 months, 4–8 months, and more than 8 months. Emotional and behavioral development was assessed using the Child Behavior Checklist 1½–5 (CBCL 1½–5).

pmc-13471582.title: Potential roles of pseudobulbs in mediating signal responses and hormone translocation during floral bud dormancy release in Pleione bulbocodioides
pmc-13471582.creator: Xiu-Mei Dong, Shi-Bao Zhang
pmc-13471582.description: Pleione bulbocodioides, a world-renowned ornamental orchid, exhibits a pronounced winter dormancy in its floral buds, thereby presenting a spring flowering characteristic. Currently, the mechanisms underlying floral bud dormancy and its release in this orchid remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the regulatory mechanism of floral bud dormancy release in P. bulbocodioides using integrated physiological and transcriptome analysis.
